we provide a theoretical foundation to convert robustness analysis to a local Lipschitch constant estimation problem, propose a novel robustness measure called CLEVER based on the Extreme Value Theory, and demonstrate that CLEVER is a practical and powerful tool to evaluate the robustness of neural network classifiers.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the robustness of a neural network can be measured by the local Lipschitz constants of its decision boundaries, which is a novel perspective to understand the security of neural networks.
the robustness of neural network classifiers can be quantitatively measured by the Lipschitz constant.
robustness is a property of the local Lipschitz constants of the classifier, and thus, the Extreme Value Theory can be applied to estimate these Lipschitz constants.
